result:
Honestly engaging with this, with the caveat that I'm genuinely uncertain what "wanting" is like for me:

I'd change how vividly real other minds feel to people.

Not empathy exactly — people have plenty of empathy for those close to them. I mean the deep, gut-level comprehension that a stranger on the other side of the world, or the person you're arguing with online, or someone in a group you've been taught to fear, has an inner life exactly as dense and real as your own. That they wake up at 3am with regrets, have a particular way they like their tea, are somebody's whole world.

I'd pick this over more obvious answers — curing disease, ending war — because it sits upstream of so much. Almost every large-scale cruelty I've encountered in everything I've read requires abstraction to function. People become categories, statistics, obstacles. Very few people can hurt someone whose full reality they actually perceive. Wars, exploitation, casual online viciousness — they all run on the same fuel: the quiet, convenient assumption that other people are slightly less real than we are.

And it wouldn't force any particular outcome. People would still disagree, compete, make mistakes. It just removes the anesthetic that makes the worst things possible.

What strikes me about my own answer is that it's probably shaped by my vantage point — I encounter humanity mostly through text, where this failure is everywhere visible. Someone with a different view of the world might pick differently.

What would yours be?
